highYieldTopics.topic: Physical science: matter, atoms, energy, waves
highYieldTopics.notes: Official GS samples test density reasoning, temperature conversion, freezing-point depression, atmospheric composition.
Atomic number = protons; periodic table periods/groups; pH scale; chemical vs physical change.
Dummies devotes an article to the scientific method; rarely a scored item type in official samples.

mustMemorise: F = (9/5)C + 32; 0 C = 32 F; 100 C = 212 F; -40 is the crossover
Air is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen (argon ~0.9%, CO2 ~0.04%)
Salt melts ice by lowering the freezing point (freezing-point depression), not by a chemical reaction
Less dense means molecules are farther apart (the official sample's stated reason)
Mitochondria = cellular respiration/ATP; chloroplast = photosynthesis; ribosome = protein synthesis; nucleus = DNA
Dominant vs recessive, genotype vs phenotype, Punnett square, DNA base pairing A-T and G-C
EM spectrum order: radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma
Three rock classes (igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic); weathering breaks rock, erosion moves it
Conduction (contact/solids), convection (fluids), radiation (no medium)
distractorPatterns: All four options are real science; one relation is wrong (e.g. 'molecules farther apart' vs 'closer together' polarity flip)
Cause vs consequence swap: a true effect offered as the cause ('it is lighter', 'it moves more quickly')
Wrong anchor value: 100 C = 32 F (the freezing point) or 200 F (doubling slip)
All-options-are-real-members: argon, neon, oxygen, nitrogen all occur in air; only the stem word 'principal' decides
Plausible-mechanism fabrication (salt 'forms an acid', 'chemically destroys water molecules')

Dummies' current cheat sheet: 'occasionally antonyms'.
Kaplan's charge technique; Mometrix lists connotation vs denotation.

mustMemorise: Roots: volu/volv turn; greg flock; loqu/locu speak; cred believe; duc/duct lead; fer carry; ject throw; mit/miss send; port carry; scrib/script write; spec/spect look; tract pull; vert/vers turn; voc call
More roots: anthrop human; chron time; geo earth; therm heat; phon sound; graph write; bio life; auto self; tele far; micro small; macro large; poly many; mono one; syn/sym together

Prefixes: a/an without; ab away; ad toward; bene good; circum around; con/com together; contra against; de down; dis apart/not; e/ex out; in/im not OR into; inter between; intra within; mal bad; mis wrong; ob against; per through; pre before; pro forward; re back/again; sub under; super above; trans across; un not
Suffixes: -tion/-sion act/noun; -ous/-ious full of; -ity/-ty state; -al/-ic relating to; -ate to make; -able/-ible capable of; -ism doctrine; -ist one who; -ize to make; -less without; -ment result

Predict the meaning before reading the options, then match or eliminate (Kaplan method)

Wrong intensity in the same semantic field (antagonize with embarrass, struggle, worship)

The antonym offered as a decoy (wilted with budding)

highYieldTopics.topic: Global questions: main idea, author's purpose, tone
highYieldTopics.notes: Kaplan names this as a common type; wrong answers are too specific, too general, contradictory or too extreme.

Official PC samples include an 'author implies' and a 'does NOT resemble' item.
Kaplan's fourth type; answer must substitute without changing meaning.
but, though, however, although, yet point to the author's view; thus, therefore, I suggest, I believe mark conclusions.
Mometrix lists cause/effect, sequence, chronological, compare/contrast, problem/solution, transition words.

highYieldTopics.topic: Critical reading: fact vs opinion, bias, fallacies
highYieldTopics.notes: Mometrix lists it; official samples do not appear to test fallacy names.
UTP's own hint: 'most nearly, most likely, usually, probably' signal best-answer, not only-true.

mustMemorise: No outside knowledge is ever needed - every answer is in the passage (Kaplan, official description)
Four question types: Global, Detail, Inference, Vocabulary-in-Context, with their stem wordings
Contrast signposts (but, though, however, although, yet) mark the author's view
Conclusion signposts (thus, therefore, I suggest, I believe) mark the main idea
Qualifier vocabulary (most nearly, most likely, usually, probably) means pick the best answer, not the only true one

distractorPatterns: True in the passage but not the answer (the official titanium item's 'does not corrode')
Too specific / too general / too extreme for Global questions
Detail answer lifted from an irrelevant part of the passage
Outside information not discussed in the passage (Inference)
Negation stem trap ('does NOT resemble') where three options restate the passage

highYieldTopics.notes: Mometrix lists all three; no official sample tests them - treat as over-scope.

mustMemorise: Units: current ampere, voltage volt, resistance ohm, power watt, energy watt-hour, frequency hertz
Ohm's law in both notations (V = IR and I = V/R) and power in all three forms (P = VI, P = I^2 R, P = V^2/R)
Series: one path, current identical, resistances add. Parallel: voltage identical, currents add, resistances reciprocate
Resistance rises with length and temperature and falls with thickness
Diode allows one-way current and rectifies AC to DC; transistor amplifies or switches; capacitor stores charge and blocks DC; inductor opposes current change; transformer changes AC voltage only
A closed circuit is required for current; a fuse or breaker opens on overload; ground is a safety return path
E is used for voltage in some ASVAB items, so read P = EI as P = VI
distractorPatterns: Sibling quantity: voltage, inductance and capacitance offered when an ohmmeter is asked about
Initialism decoys that fit the letters (AC offered as 'additional charge', 'alternating coil', 'ampere current')
Reversed-polarity pair: 'requires less operating power' vs 'requires more operating power', plus the obsolete-tube comparison
Reciprocal or fraction slip around V/R (one-third, one-half, 1, 3 amperes for a 2-ohm resistor)

A countersink bevels the hole mouth so a screw head sits flush; a twist drill makes the hole; an auger bit bores deep in wood; a cold chisel cuts cold metal

mustMemorise: Two item families: connection (dot and line) and fit-together (jigsaw)
Rotation is legal, reflection is not - a mirrored option is always wrong

For connection items the discriminating features are the dot's position and where the line enters or exits the shape
Eliminate any option containing a part you were not given, or missing a notch you were given

commonGuideErrors: Dummies' live 'Breakdown of the ASVAB Subtests' page (Rod Powers, updated 2016-07-24) still publishes 16-item CAT counts and 8-minute GS/WK/EI limits; official is 15 items, 12/9/10 minutes. https://www.dummies.com/article/academics-the-arts/study-skills-test-prep/armed-services/breakdown-of-the-asvab-subtests-169176/
The same 2016 page still names Coding Speed as a live subtest 'for a few Navy jobs'.

Kaplan's ASVAB Math Strategies page gives AR 42 minutes and MK 23 minutes; official is 55 and 31. The 23 matches the retired 2020 official figure. https://www.kaptest.com/study/asvab/asvab-math-strategies/
Kaplan's own site still links to 'Kaplan ASVAB 2018-2019 Prep Plus' in its navigation, evidence of pages frozen years ago.

Dummies tells candidates the CAT does not penalise guessing 'unless you're making a lot of guesses at the end of a computerized subtest'; the official 2026 fact sheet says the CAT-ASVAB has a penalty for guessing.
Dummies describes PC passages as 'usually a few hundred words'; Kaplan says 30-120 words and the official samples are two to four sentences.
Achievable's AFQT percentages (AR 27-29%, WK 27-33%) are shares of AFQT QUESTIONS, not of score; because VE is doubled, verbal is about 55.6% of AFQT raw weight and AR/MK 16.7% each.
Achievable states '135-150 questions' and '3 hours 17+ minutes' for the CAT; official is 135 items and 197 minutes of limits.
Achievable, Mometrix and others still publish per-branch AFQT minimums without a date, which drift whenever a branch changes policy; the Program publishes no such table.
Peterson's Master the ASVAB in print is the 23rd edition dated May 2018, i.e. written under pre-2020 CAT time limits; it is not a 2024-2026 source.
No 2024-2026 McGraw-Hill ASVAB edition could be located (2023 product is the newest found), so any 'current' McGraw-Hill citation should be treated as 2023.

Union Test Prep's ASVAB formula sheet teaches standard deviation, variance, coefficient of variation, conditional probability, arithmetic and geometric sequences and logarithms, none of which appear in official samples or in any guide's own scope list.

Free line-score and composite-formula pages still circulate formulas containing Numerical Operations (NO) and Coding Speed (CS), two subtests retired from the CAT-ASVAB; only GT = VE + AR is consistently defensible.
Barron's 14th-edition blurb says '7 full-length practice tests - 4 in the book and 4 online' (4+4 = 8), showing vendor copy is unaudited.

Mometrix's free checklists include graduate-adjacent topics (Kirchhoff's laws, Bernoulli, Hooke, permutations and combinations) that over-scope the real test and can waste a candidate's remaining study time.
Study.com's ASVAB pages could not be read at all (CAPTCHA), so nothing attributed to Study.com should be presented as verified.
The official 2024 fact sheet itself printed a total of 198 minutes while its own subtest times summed to 197; guides that copied it inherited the error.
